source.text: ወበ*እማንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ሚጠት፡ ትከውን፡ *ለቅዱሳን፡ ወለኅሩያን፡ ወብርሃነ፡ መዋዕል፡ ዲቤሆሙ፡ የኀድር፡ ወስብሐት፡ ወክብር፡ ለቅዱሳን፡ ይትመየጥ፡ [በዕለት፡ እንተ፡ ጻሕብ፡

translation.text: In those days a change will come for the holy and chosen ones.[a] The light of days will rest upon them, and glory and honor will turn toward the holy ones. [On the day of distress,[b]

footnotes.text: Dillmann’s1865 lexicon, column216, explicitly cites50:1 for change/transformation (mutatio,immutatio). This word is not silently replaced with mercy or compassion.

Charles’s interpolation bracket begins here and continues into verse2. Printed93 note6 calls the passage corrupt or interpolated and brackets it as the latter. The provisional English preserves its distress/evil-storage terms without claiming that the damaged syntax or antiquity is resolved.

source.text: ዘተዘገበ፡ እኪተ፡ ላዕለ፡ ኃጥኣን፡] ወይመውኡ፡ ጻድቃን፡ በ*ስሙ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ወ*ያርኢ፡ ለካልኣን፡ ከመ፡ ይኔስሑ፡ ወይኅድጉ፡ ምግባረ፡ እደዊሆሙ።

translation.text: evil has been stored up against sinners.][a] The righteous will prevail in the name of the Lord of Spirits, and he will show others that they should repent and abandon the works of their hands.[b]

footnotes.text: This closing bracket continues the problematic passage from verse1. The selected form speaks of evil stored up against sinners, but the whole construction is marked corrupt or interpolated by Charles printed93 note6; this is an annotated provisional rendering, not a silent repair from another edition.

The selected main text has the showing verb; printed93 note11 records differing forms and a possible corruption. The English retains its unexpressed third-person agent rather than importing a named agent or a different verb.

source.text: ወ*ኢ፡ ይከውን፡ ሎሙ፡ ክብር፡ በቅድመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ወበስሙ፡ ይድኅኑ፡ ወእግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ይምሕሮሙ፡ እስመ፡ ብዙኅ፡ ምሕረቱ።

translation.text: They will have no honor before the Lord of Spirits,[a] but in his name they will be saved, and the Lord of Spirits will have mercy on them, because his mercy is great.

footnotes.text: The selected printed text explicitly includes the negativeኢ, no/not; Charles printed93 note14 records its omission in some manuscripts. The negative is retained alongside the following promise of salvation and mercy rather than harmonized away.

source.text: ወ*ጻድቅ፡ ውእቱ፡ ወበኵነኔሁ፡ ወበቅድመ፡ *ስብሐት፡ ዚአሁ፡ ወዐመፃ፡ ኢትቀውም፡ በኵነኔሁ፡ ዘኢይኔስሕ፡ ቅድሜሁ፡ ይትሀጐል።

translation.text: He is righteous in his judgment and before his glory.[a] Unrighteousness will not stand in his judgment; whoever does not repent will perish before him.

footnotes.text: The selected wording’s coordination of righteous, judgment and before his glory is compressed. This English retains those elements and the following no-standing/no-repentance clauses; it does not claim to resolve every syntactic relation. Charles printed93 notes20-24 record differing readings and a possible repeated phrase.

translation.text: “From now on he will not show them mercy,” says the Lord of Spirits.[a]

footnotes.text: The printed verb is third person; it is not silently changed to I in the quoted declaration. Its negative is also retained rather than reconciled with verse3.

source.text: ወበእማንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ *ታገብእ፡ ምድር፡ ማሕፀንታ፡ ወሲኦል፡ ታገብእ፡ ዘተመጠወት፡ ወሀጕል፡ ያገብእ፡ ዘይፈዲ።

translation.text: In those days the earth will give back what was entrusted to it,[a] and Sheol will give back what it was given, and Destruction[b] will give back what it owes.[c]

footnotes.text: The selected noun means a deposit or entrusted charge, not a womb. Dillmann1865 columns138-139 explicitly cites51:1 under depositum, including entrusted persons as well as things. This does not supply an absent phrase from another text.
Sheol is the realm of the dead. Destruction renders the place-of-destruction noun; Dillmann1865 column19 explicitly cites51:1 for that underworld sense (Abaddon), not a separate named being.
The debt/restitution verb is supported by Dillmann1865 column1379, which cites51:1 under owing something. All three return clauses are retained.

source.text: ወየኀሪ፡ ጻድቃነ፡ ወቅዱሳነ፡ እምኔሆሙ፡ እስመ፡ ቀርበት፡ ዕለት፡ ከመ፡ እሙንቱ፡ ይድኅኑ።

translation.text: He will choose the righteous and holy from among them, for the day has drawn near for them to be saved.

source.text: ወኅሩይ፡ በእማንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ዲበ፡ መንበሩ፡ ይነብር፡ ወኵሎ፡ ኅሊናተ፡ ጥበብ፡ ወ†እምኅሊና፡ አፉሁ፡ የወፅእ፡ እስመ፡ እግዚአ፡ መንፈሳት፡ ወሀቦ፡ ወሰብሖ።

translation.text: In those days the Chosen One will sit on his throne, and he will bring forth all thoughts of wisdom from the thought of his mouth,[a] because the Lord of Spirits has given it to him and glorified him.[b]

footnotes.text: The printed dagger marks a corrupt phrase beginning with from the thought. Charles printed94 note11 proposes different emendations and moving the preposition; none is silently installed here. The awkward expression is preserved in a provisional English construal, not certified as a recovered original reading.
The object of has given is not expressed in the selected Ge’ez; it is left as it in English rather than specified as a new gift not stated by the text.

source.text: በእማንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ይዘፍኑ፡ አድባር፡ ከመ፡ ሐራጊት፡ ወአውግር፡ ያንፈርዕፁ፡ ከመ፡ መሐስእ፡ ጽጉባነ፡ ሐሊብ፡ ወይከውኑ፡ ኵሎ፡ መላእክት፡ በሰማይ፡ ገጾሙ፡ የበርሁ፡ በፍሥሓ።

translation.text: In those days the mountains will dance like vines, and the hills will leap like calves full of milk. All the angels in heaven will have faces shining with joy.[a]

footnotes.text: The final angels/faces construction is unusual. Charles printed94 notes20 and22 discuss taking angels as the subject and combining the be and shine verbs. This English follows that disclosed syntactic construal; it does not turn the mountains or hills into angels.

source.text: እስመ፡ በእማንቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ኅሩይ፡ ተንሥአ፡ ወምድር፡ ትትፌሣሕ፡ ወጻድቃን፡ ዲቤሃ፡ የኀድሩ፡ ወኅሩያን፡ ዲቤሃ፡ የሐውሩ፡ [ወይትፌሣሑ፡]።

translation.text: For in those days the Chosen One has arisen, and the earth will rejoice. The righteous will dwell upon it, and the chosen will walk upon it [and rejoice].[a]

footnotes.text: Charles brackets the final and rejoice as dittography in printed94 note28. It is retained visibly in brackets here, not presented as an uncontested separate clause.
